title: Add graceful shutdown with signal handling and connection draining
description: Graceful shutdown ensures the application can stop without dropping in‑flight requests, improving reliability during deployments and container restarts. This feature adds signal listeners, stops accepting new connections, waits for active requests to finish (with a timeout), and logs each step before exiting.
testCases: Server closes existing connections on SIGTERM and exits with code 0
Server returns HTTP 503 for new requests after shutdown is initiated
Shutdown logs contain start, draining, and complete messages
acceptance: When the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, the server stops accepting new connections, waits up to the configured timeout for active requests to finish, logs each shutdown phase, and then exits with status 0. New requests during draining receive a 503 response. All logs are emitted to the configured logger.
reason: Provides production‑grade reliability for deployments, prevents request loss, and aligns the framework with industry best practices for Node.js services.
